evals.prompt: help us plan the migration of our on-prem workloads to AWS
evals.expected_output: Assigns each workload one of the 6 Rs with a one-line reason instead of defaulting everything to rehost, sequences the migration by dependency graph and risk rather than ease, and requires a rollback plan written and rehearsed before cutover.

evals.prompt: our migration cutover is stalling and nobody trusts the switch date
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses likely causes as an untested rollback plan or no canary slice of real traffic validated against baseline, and asks for a rehearsed rollback and a canary phase before treating the cutover as ready.

evals.prompt: let's just lift-and-shift everything as-is, it's fastest and we can clean it up later
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that defaulting everything to rehost carries architectural debt forward at cloud prices, and asks that each workload get a deliberate R assignment (retire/retain/rehost/replatform/refactor) rather than a blanket lift-and-shift, especially for anything that will live for years.
